Hi, I found a reproducible IME issue with the new ChatGPT Linux preview.

Environment:

  * ChatGPT Linux: 26.803.81509
  * EndeavourOS (Arch Linux), x86_64
  * KDE Plasma / KWin Wayland
  * Fcitx5 with Korean input
  * Installed through the AUR package `openai-chatgpt`, which repackages the official OpenAI `.deb` binary



Issue:

When ChatGPT is launched normally, the Korean Hangul/English toggle key does not work inside the ChatGPT app.

Fcitx5 itself is working normally, and the same Hangul/English toggle key works correctly in other applications on the same system.

I found that launching ChatGPT with the following flags fixes the problem immediately:

`chatgpt --enable-features=UseOzonePlatform --ozone-platform=wayland --enable-wayland-ime`

After launching ChatGPT this way:

  * the Hangul/English toggle key works normally
  * Korean input works normally



Steps to reproduce:

  1. Launch ChatGPT normally.

  2. Focus the message input field.

  3. Press the Hangul/English toggle key.

  4. The input method does not switch to Korean.

  5. Quit ChatGPT.

  6. Launch ChatGPT with:

`chatgpt --enable-features=UseOzonePlatform --ozone-platform=wayland --enable-wayland-ime`

  7. Focus the message input field again.

  8. Press the same Hangul/English toggle key.

  9. Korean input now works correctly.




Expected behavior:

ChatGPT should work with the active Wayland/Fcitx5 input method when launched normally, without requiring additional command-line flags.

I understand that EndeavourOS / Arch Linux is not currently an officially supported distribution. However, since the issue disappears simply by enabling the Wayland IME flags while using the same ChatGPT binary, this may indicate an issue with the app’s default Wayland/IME configuration rather than Fcitx5 itself.

I have reproduced this specifically with Korean input. It may also be worth checking whether other Fcitx5 or CJK IME configurations on Wayland are affected.

Thanks!
external.title: Wayland IME issue with Fcitx5 (Korean input) in ChatGPT Linux app

Hi OpenAI team,

I wanted to share a pricing idea based on a problem I suspect many ChatGPT users have.

I use ChatGPT a lot and would genuinely benefit from the Pro model, but the individual Pro subscription is difficult to justify financially, especially when I probably wouldn’t use its full capacity every day.

What I would love to see is something like a **“Pro Family” or “Shared Pro Capacity” plan** : several people could pay together for a larger pool of Pro usage, while still keeping completely separate accounts, conversations, memories, and personal data.

For example, instead of one person paying the full Pro price, five users could each contribute a smaller amount and share an overall usage allowance.

I think this could solve an interesting pricing gap: there are probably many Plus users who would never upgrade individually to Pro, but who would happily pay more than Plus if they could access Pro through a shared plan. That could potentially increase revenue per user while making the higher-end models accessible to more people.

Basically: **share the computing allowance, not the account.**

I previously had a similar thought about shared subscription models, so apparently I have now started giving companies product ideas for free.

At this point, if you end up implementing it, I suppose you also owe me a job.

Thanks for reading, and for building a product I use enough to spend my free time thinking about its pricing model.

Best,
Kevin
external.title: A “Pro Family” / Shared Pro Capacity Plan

external.description: A crab trapped by its own growth exposes an overlooked hazard of floating plastic waste. That puzzle led Hiroshima University researchers to reconstruct how the animal entered the bottle, what it ate, and how it survived long enough to outgrow its only exit.
